title: Large-Scale Compliance Data Repair
subtitle: 100M+ records · $2.5M fine avoided · Bank of America
description: Saved the company an expected $2.5 million compliance fine from FINRA by repairing +100 million preprocessed records having absent or incorrect fields/attributes of FIX messages through a Python automation process. Led the migration of legacy components to modern technologies.
narrative: Fixed data and automated processes to help the bank avoid millions in compliance fines — utilized FIX protocol's enrichment logic to curate strategies to better serve the automation.
modal_about:
As a Software Engineer II at Bank of America, I led the repair of 100+ million preprocessed trade records with absent or incorrect FIX message fields — data quality failures that were exposing the firm to a projected $2.5M FINRA compliance fine.

I engineered a Python automation pipeline that leveraged FIX protocol enrichment logic to identify, flag, and correct malformed records at scale. I also drove the migration of several legacy components to modern technologies, improving maintainability and reducing toil.
_note: Résumé-safe description only. No proprietary system names.

title: Copyright Laundering in Agentic AIs
subtitle: Research · LLM behavior · IP policy · Apr–May 2026
description: Investigated how agentic AI systems can inadvertently (or deliberately) reproduce copyrighted material through multi-step reasoning chains — a form of laundering that bypasses single-inference detection. Analyzed model behavior, proposed detection heuristics, and mapped gaps in current AI policy frameworks.
narrative: What happens when a chain of 'safe' steps produces an unsafe output? This project tried to answer that for intellectual property.
modal_about:
Large language models are regularly tested for single-step copyright reproduction — but what about multi-step agentic chains where each individual step appears safe?

This research investigates how agentic AI systems can inadvertently (or deliberately) reproduce copyrighted material through sequences of 'safe' intermediate steps — a pattern I call copyright laundering. I analyzed model behavior across several architectures, proposed detection heuristics for identifying laundering patterns, and mapped the gaps in current AI policy frameworks that leave this vector unaddressed.

title: ODD Gaming Toxicity Detection
subtitle: NLP · Online harm · Real-time classification
description: Built a toxicity detection system for online gaming environments using transformer-based classification. Addressed class imbalance, context-dependent slang, and low-latency requirements.
narrative: Language in games is its own dialect — abbreviations, irony, in-group jargon. Off-the-shelf models fail fast.
modal_about:
Online gaming communities generate massive volumes of text with unique linguistic patterns — abbreviations, irony, in-group slang, and context-dependent insults that defeat off-the-shelf moderation models.

I built a toxicity detection classifier tailored to gaming environments using transformer-based models, with specific handling for class imbalance (toxic content is a small fraction of overall chat), context-dependent slang, and the low-latency requirements of real-time applications. The project explored what it takes to make NLP actually work in a specialized, noisy domain.

title: SnapEat
subtitle: Google AI Hackathon · Menu AI · Apr–May 2024
description: Built a full-stack web application using React and Django that leverages Gemini AI to parse and analyze user-submitted images of menus, generating personalized dish recommendations from 100s of menu items with 90%+ accuracy.
narrative: Photo → menu → recommendations in under a second. The engineering was less about ML and more about making the demo feel effortless.
modal_about:
Built for the Google AI Hackathon, SnapEat is a full-stack web application that turns a photo of a restaurant menu into personalized dish recommendations.

Users snap a photo of any menu — handwritten, laminated, printed — and SnapEat uses Google Gemini 1.5 Pro to parse every item, extract descriptions and prices, and generate tailored recommendations based on dietary preferences and taste profiles. The pipeline achieves 90%+ accuracy across diverse menu formats.

Built with React on the front end, Django on the back end, and deployed on Azure. The biggest challenge was making the vision-to-recommendation pipeline fast enough to feel instant.

title: Cartier Jewelry Recommender: Maison de Bijoux
subtitle: Generative AI · K-Modes Clustering · Nov–Dec 2025
description: Built a jewelry recommendation system for Cartier using K-Modes clustering and generative AI to match customers to pieces based on style, occasion, and preference signals.
narrative: Fashion recommendation meets unsupervised learning — clustering across categorical features where Euclidean distance means nothing.
modal_about:
Traditional recommender systems rely on Euclidean distance — but jewelry preference is inherently categorical. Metal type, stone, style, occasion, and price tier don't live on a number line.

For Cartier's Maison de Bijoux project, I applied K-Modes clustering to group customers by categorical preference signals, then used generative AI to generate natural-language explanations of why a given piece was recommended for a given cluster profile. The result is a recommendation experience that feels curated rather than algorithmic.

title: Daily Feedback Intelligence Report Agent
subtitle: Agentic AI · Cloudflare · Data Analytics · Jan 2026
description: Built an autonomous agent that generates daily feedback intelligence reports by aggregating, analyzing, and synthesizing user feedback signals into actionable product insights.
narrative: Turning noisy feedback streams into a daily brief — the kind of report a PM would want on their desk every morning without having to ask.
modal_about:
Product teams drown in feedback — app reviews, support tickets, NPS surveys, social mentions — with no consistent way to surface what actually matters each day.

This agent runs autonomously every morning: it ingests feedback signals from multiple sources, clusters them by theme, detects sentiment shifts and emerging issues, and synthesizes everything into a structured daily intelligence report. Built on Cloudflare's edge infrastructure for low-latency, always-on operation.

title: Impact of Twin Lockdowns on Hunger, Labor Market Outcomes, and Household Coping Mechanisms
subtitle: Econometrics research · Uganda · Dickinson College · Feb–May 2021
description: Examined the economic impact of COVID-19 lockdown policies on household livelihoods in Uganda. Applied difference-in-differences estimation to panel survey data, controlling for pre-trend confounders. Published on SSRN.
narrative: The hardest part was the data — survey data from a low-income context with significant missingness. The methodology had to be transparent about its limits.
modal_about:
Uganda experienced two distinct COVID-19 lockdowns in 2020–2021. This research examines their differential impact on household food security, labor market participation, and coping mechanisms using panel survey data from the Uganda High-Frequency Phone Survey.

I applied difference-in-differences estimation across lockdown periods, controlling for pre-trend confounders and accounting for significant data missingness endemic to low-income survey contexts. Findings were published on SSRN.

title: Digital vs. Physical Music Revenue During Recessions
subtitle: Time-series analysis · Music Industry · Feb–May 2021
description: Analyzed the independent level of digital and physical format revenues of the recorded music industry during recessions using multivariable regression and time-series analysis.
narrative: Music economics at the intersection of data and the industry I care about — what happens to streaming when the economy contracts?
modal_about:
Does the music industry follow the broader economy, or does it move counter-cyclically? And does the answer differ between digital and physical formats?

This project analyzes RIAA revenue data across multiple recession periods, applying multivariable regression and time-series techniques to isolate the independent behavior of digital streaming, digital downloads, and physical sales. Results suggest digital and physical formats respond very differently to economic downturns — with implications for how the industry should think about format diversification.

title: Hackathons & Competitions
subtitle: Rossmann Store Sales · Facebook Data Challenge · and others
description: Competed in multiple data science challenges including the Rossmann Store Sales Forecast competition on Kaggle (Jul–Aug 2020) and the Facebook Data Challenge. Applied forecasting, feature engineering, and ensemble methods across varied problem domains.
narrative: Competitions taught me to iterate fast — a working model in 6 hours is more useful than a perfect one in 6 weeks.
modal_about:
A collection of competitive data science work:

**Rossmann Store Sales Forecast (Kaggle, Jul–Aug 2020)** — Forecasted daily sales for 1,115 Rossmann drug stores across Germany. Applied XGBoost with extensive feature engineering on store metadata, promotions, and seasonality signals.

**Facebook Data Challenge** — Analyzed social network behavior patterns using large-scale graph data.

Competitions remain the fastest way I know to develop judgment about what actually moves the needle on a problem.
